page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.large is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor clocked at 3.5 GHz, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 dedicated vCPUs via hyperthreading. The processor features 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache, supporting vector acceleration features including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also bundles 118 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no GPUs on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the operational characteristics of this dual-thread configuration. Single-threaded performance sits firmly in the middle tier, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1610.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1882.48. Compression speeds also maintain average metrics, reaching 28.0 GB/sec in gzip single-threaded tests. However, overall multi-core and aggregate compute metrics reflect the limitations of having only two vCPUs. The Geekbench multi-core score of 1836.0, stress-ng multi-core score of 1924.78, and PassMark CPU score of 2964.98 place in the lowest percentiles across general infrastructure testing.

Memory throughput and storage characteristics reflect its hardware allocation. Cached small-block memory reads yield 103.28 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measure 14.54 GB/sec and 13.51 GB/sec respectively. PassMark memory testing scored 1761.55, and Redis SET throughput recorded 1.93 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput peaked at 3.22 GB/sec. For lightweight AI tasks, prompt processing reached 204.78 tokens per second and text generation reached 56.65 tokens per second on a small 135M model.

The primary tradeoff of the r6idn.large lies between compute throughput and resource balance. While multi-threaded parallel throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU count, the instance couples 16 GB of system RAM with fast local NVMe SSD storage. This design delivers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy or caching tasks that do not demand extensive CPU concurrency. Best-fit workloads include small Redis or memcached instances, lightweight in-memory databases, caching proxy servers, and development or staging environments requiring local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r6idn.large is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core) running at 3.5 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory (an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio) and 118 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, backed by a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance demonstrates solid single-threaded capabilities with a Geekbench single-core score of 1610.0 and 28.0 GB/sec gzip compression throughput. However, aggregate compute and multi-core benchmark results place in lower tiers due to the dual-thread ceiling. Incorporating local NVMe storage with an ample RAM footprint makes r6idn.large suitable for memory-intensive caching tiers, lightweight in-memory databases, and applications requiring rapid transient local storage without heavy multi-threaded compute demands.
